test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 2, 5 and 20 days, respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do thrice the same work, working together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency: A = 1/2, B = 1/5, C = 1/20

Total efficiency = 1/2 + 1/5 + 1/20 = 10/20 + 4/20 + 1/20 = 15/20 = 3/4

Time for 1 work = 1 ÷ (3/4) = 4/3 days

Time for 3 works = 3 × (4/3) = 4 days

**∴ The correct answer is 4 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Total efficiency = 10 + 4 + 1 = 15 units/day

⇒ Time for 1 work = 20 ÷ 15 = 4/3 days

⇒ Time for 3 works = 3 × (4/3) = 4 days

**∴ The correct answer is 4 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method

Take LCM of days as total work. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Days.

Combined Work Formula

If efficiencies are a, b, c then total = a + b + c and Time = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency.

Multiple Work Concept

If 1 work takes T days, then n works take n × T days.

Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time: Efficiency ∝ 1/Time.
